headline_answer.question: Is 'compute or measure the target elsewhere, then hand a model to the channel simulator' the standards-track approach?
headline_answer.verdict: YES, and not loosely - it is written into the specification. 3GPP TR 38.901 V19.4.0 clause 7.9.2.1 'RCS of a sensing target' defines the target signature as sigma_RCS = sigma_M * sigma_D * sigma_S, ships the numbers as Tables 7.9.2.1-1 through -7, and multiplies them into the simulated channel in two named places: the per-path power in Step 10 and the target-channel scaling in Step 15 of clause 7.9.4.1. Nothing in the channel generator computes a scattering integral; the sigma arrives from outside as a parameter set. By the definition in force here (signature computed OUTSIDE the propagation simulator, then applied to simulated paths as sigma) the 3GPP ISAC channel model IS injection, and it is the mainstream, not a fringe workaround.
headline_answer.who_computes_the_table_in_the_standards_: A pooled mix. Of the 38 target-signature evidence rows the moderator collected in R1-2504948, 27 are measurement campaigns, 9 are ray-tracing simulations and 2 are commercial EM-solver simulations (machine count by me from the attached xlsx). Both routes - measurement and external solver - were admitted on equal footing, and the final standardized numbers are an AVERAGE ACROSS COMPANIES of both.
headline_answer.consequence_for_our_positioning: Our sigma grid (9 el x 120 az x 3 bands per airframe, computed by our own SBR+PO on Sionna's ray engine, then multiplied into simulated paths) is the same architecture as the standard's, differing only in that we keep the full angular grid instead of collapsing it to a fitted pattern, and we keep a frequency axis, which 3GPP dropped.
headline_answer.one_thing_reviewers_will_still_ask: Not 'why inject' - that fight is over. They will ask what the injected number was checked against. Every strong instance answers that question; the 3GPP spec itself answers it only by pointing at a company source list.

the_injection_model_as_printed.decomposition_quote: The RCS related coefficient sigma_RCS of a SPST for a pair of incident/scattered angles is composed of a first component sigma_M which is included in the large-scale parameters (described in Step 15 in Clause 7.9.4.1), and a second component sigma_D and third component sigma_S which are both included in the small-scale parameters (described in Step 10 in Clause 7.9.4.1), i.e., sigma_RCS = sigma_M sigma_D sigma_S. sigma_M is a deterministic value for the SPST. sigma_D can be fixed to 1 or can be angular dependent. sigma_S follows log-normal distribution.
the_injection_model_as_printed.component_meanings: sigma_M = deterministic mean linear monostatic RCS; sigma_D = deterministic angular pattern; sigma_S = log-normal random component with mu_dB = -(ln10/20) * sigma_dB^2 (eq. 7.9.2-1), i.e. constrained so the linear mean is preserved.
the_injection_model_as_printed.rcs_model_1_equation_7.9.2-2: sigma_MD_dB(theta_i,phi_i,theta_s,phi_s) = max( 10lg(sigma_M) - 3 sin(beta/2), sigma_FS(...) ), where beta in [0,180] is the bistatic angle and sigma_FS (forward scattering) is set to -infinity.
the_injection_model_as_printed.rcs_model_2_equation_7.9.2-3: sigma_MD_dB = max( G_max - min( -(sigma_VdB(theta)+sigma_HdB(phi)), sigma_max - k1 sin^k2(beta/2) + 5 log10 cos(beta/2) ), G_max - sigma_max, sigma_FS ), with sigma_VdB / sigma_HdB the 3GPP-style parabolic beam terms in zenith and azimuth about (theta_center, phi_center) with 3 dB widths, and k1/k2 per target: k1=6.05,k2=1.33 (UAV large), k1=0.5714,k2=0.1 (human model 2), k1=6,k2=1.65 (vehicle), k1=12,k2=1.45 (AGV).
the_injection_model_as_printed.the_lookup_step_quote: For a ST with single scattering point, N_sp >= 1 sets of parameters phi_center, phi_3dB, theta_center, theta_3dB, G_max, sigma_max, Range of theta and Range of phi are defined. The bisector angle (theta,phi) is used to index one set from the N_sp sets of parameters, and determine sigma_MD_dB(theta_i,phi_i,theta_s,phi_s) of the ST consequently.
the_injection_model_as_printed.note_this_is_a_lookup: Index-by-angle-sector into a parameter table is exactly the table-lookup step of injection; the table is compressed into sector parameters rather than shipped as raw dBsm per angle.

where_the_sigma_multiplies_in.step_10_quote: Step 10: Obtain the power for all generated paths. The power of a path is given by (7.9.4-1) where (sigma_D, sigma_S) are the second and third component of RCS at the SPST p for a path are derived by the incident angle, i.e., AOA, ZOA of the ray in the STX-SPST link and the scattered angle, i.e., AOD, ZOD of the ray in the SPST-SRX link, referring to the RCS model defined in Clause 7.9.2.1 for the SPST.
where_the_sigma_multiplies_in.step_15_quote: Step 15: Apply pathloss, shadowing, the first component of RCS for the channel coefficients. The target channel for ST k is formed by summing the channel coefficients of the P SPST respectively scaled by the pathloss, shadowing and the first component of RCS sigma_M of the P SPST.
where_the_sigma_multiplies_in.coupling_loss_formula_in_calibration_tab: L_TX-SPST-RX = PL_dB(d1) + PL_dB(d2) + 10lg( (c/(4 pi f))^2 )^-1 - 10lg(sigma_RCS,A) + SF_dB,1 + SF_dB,2  (as printed in Table 7.9.6.1-1; the sign convention is the bistatic radar equation with the RCS entering as a subtraction from loss)
where_the_sigma_multiplies_in.plain_reading: The channel generator never solves for scattering. It generates two link geometries (Tx-target and target-Rx), couples their rays, and multiplies in a sigma that was determined elsewhere. That is injection.

what_the_standard_deliberately_left_out.no_frequency_axis: The standardized sigma_M values carry no frequency argument. -12.81 dBsm is used across the TR's whole 0.5-100 GHz scope. The calibration tables (7.9.6.1-1) apply the same -12.81 dBsm at FR1 6 GHz and FR2 30 GHz.
what_the_standard_deliberately_left_out.mono_equals_bi_in_calibration: Table 7.9.6.1-1 prints, for the UAV case: 'The same values are used for monostatic RCS and bistatic RCS' (the bistatic dependence enters only through the -3 sin(beta/2) / k1,k2 terms of the model, not through separate parameters).
what_the_standard_deliberately_left_out.far_field_only: Clause 4 applicability list: 'The sensing target is assumed in the far field of the sensing transmitter/receiver for the channel model(s) for ISAC in Clause 7.9.'
what_the_standard_deliberately_left_out.why_this_matters_to_us: Our grid keeps both axes the standard collapsed - angle (9 x 120 samples rather than 6 sectors) and frequency (3 bands rather than one number). Against the standard we are strictly finer-grained, which is a defensible position, not a deficiency.

how_the_number_was_actually_produced.what_this_means: The de-facto community default sigma for a small UAV is a consensus arithmetic average over a heterogeneous pool - anechoic measurements, ray-tracing runs and commercial EM-solver runs - and one contributor (BUPT) even supplied a frequency-dependent formula that the average threw away. This is the single most useful fact in this report: the number everyone injects was itself produced by averaging simulated and measured signatures together.

external_solver_evidence_inside_the_stan.quote: The simulation is performed using software CST Studio Suite with ray tracing as solver. The signal source was assumed to be in far-field location, with the carrier frequency set to 3.5 GHz. In the simulation, the four different polarized RCS components: RCS_V-V, RCS_H-H, RCS_V-H, RCS_H-V, along with the co-polarization and cross-polarization phases are generated. Additionally, to study the angle dependency, we simulated the RCS at different azimuth angles theta and zenith angles phi, with the angular granularity of 1 degree.
external_solver_evidence_inside_the_stan.target: x-copter class UAV mesh scaled to 0.4m x 0.3m x 0.2m, 'assumed to be made of metal with a homogeneous surface'
external_solver_evidence_inside_the_stan.products: Table 1 of R1-2500660: A = -19.78 dBsm, B1 = 0 dB, std(B2) = 6.01 dB, alpha_i,1 (v-v) 0 dB, alpha_i,2 (h-h) -0.25 dB, beta_i,1 (v-h) -5.37 dB; plus a fitted RCS angular correlation corr(theta) = exp(-dtheta/theta_corr) with theta_corr = 6.87 deg for the small UAV.
external_solver_evidence_inside_the_stan.discrepancy_recorded: The moderator's validation sheet labels both Sony rows 'EM simulation based on Method of moments (MoM)', but Sony's own documents say CST Studio Suite with a RAY-TRACING solver. Quote both; do not describe Sony's input as MoM on this evidence.
external_solver_evidence_inside_the_stan.why_it_matters_to_us: A commercial EM solver's 1-degree RCS grid of a metal drone mesh was submitted to, discussed in, and averaged into a 3GPP specification. That is the exact operation our SBR+PO pipeline performs, done by a standards participant, accepted by the standards process.

external_solver_evidence_inside_the_stan.quote: To verify the angle dependency of parameters B1/B2, we conducted a simulation using a large UAV model (1600 x 1600 x 300 mm) in the HFSS simulator [4] with simulation setup as shown in Figure 10. The results indicate that, for the large UAV, a more jagged RCS pattern with large variance emerges as the elevation angle increases...
external_solver_evidence_inside_the_stan.reference_as_printed: [4] ANSYS, Inc. 'Getting Started with HFSS: Radar Cross Section', January 2020
external_solver_evidence_inside_the_stan.note: The validation sheet files Samsung's UAV rows as 'RT simulation'; the document names Ansys HFSS for the large-UAV angular study. Both are external solvers.

external_solver_evidence_inside_the_stan.quote: Our RT simulation results also exhibit that large fluctuation occurs between adjacent angle, e.g., human monostatic RCS with 1 degree simulation step.
Although from our measurement and electromagnetic simulations, there is quite a lot of fluctuation in the value of the RCS across angle, we think this is a lower priority issue.

Moreover, the current RCS modeling approach in RAN1 is based on stochastic characteristics derived from companies' measurement and ray-tracing results. Introducing angular correlation in this context would not align with the philosophy of defining RCS as a stochastic characteristic.
external_solver_evidence_inside_the_stan.why_it_matters: A one-sentence, in-record statement that the standard's RCS is derived from measurement AND ray-tracing results. If a reviewer challenges the legitimacy of a ray-traced signature, this is the sentence to put in front of them.

external_solver_evidence_inside_the_stan.quote: Option 2: Experimental results to validate a ray-tracing model, then the ray-tracing based results to validate the ISAC channel model.
external_solver_evidence_inside_the_stan.also: Proposal 24: RAN1 to study how to validate ISAC channel, e.g., real-world measurement, ray tracing, hybrid method.
external_solver_evidence_inside_the_stan.why_it_matters: This is the validation chain we should adopt verbatim: measurement validates the ray tracer; the validated ray tracer validates the channel/detection model. It was proposed inside 3GPP, by a major vendor, for exactly this problem.

external_solver_evidence_inside_the_stan.quote: If companies don't observe any continuity in B2 it is clear evidence that that their measurements are done with too coarse angular sampling. While it is common understanding that B1 captures slower variations of the RCS over angle, the variations captured by B2 are fast, but not infinitely fast.
external_solver_evidence_inside_the_stan.why_it_matters: An adversarial reading of our own grid: 3 degrees in azimuth, 9 elevations. Ericsson's argument says angular sampling that is too coarse manufactures apparent randomness. We should be able to state our angular correlation length (Sony measured 6.87 deg for a small UAV) against our 3 degree azimuth step.

the_key_sentence_for_us.quote: In the top-down approach, the RCS model is generated based on measuring the ratio between the scattered and incident electric fields from the object. The values of the scattered and incident electric fields can be obtained from measurement campaigns, numerical simulations, or ray-tracing tools.
the_key_sentence_for_us.reading: A standards body puts ray-tracing tools on the same line as measurement campaigns as an admissible source of the target RCS model. This is the cleanest published sentence licensing our route.

other_quotes.quote: To obtain practical results, bottom-up approach may calibrate the generated RCS model using the obtained results from measurement campaigns or electromagnetic numerical simulations.
The evaluated object RCS using segmentation can be further calibrated through either measurement results or electromagnetic numerical simulation tools such CST.

other_quotes.clause: 5.2.9 Views on RCS incorporation in ETSI TR 138 901
other_quotes.quote: Figure 5.2-4 highlights the amended blocks to integrate the RCS model with its two components RCS_LS and RCS_SS. The first amended block is the Path Loss (PL) model to integrate the slow-fading component of the RCS as: PL_dB = PL_dB - A_dBsm ... The last block to be amended is the channel coefficient generation, where the RCS_SS two components can be integrated into equations (7.5-28) and (7.5-29) in ETSI TR 138 901 in the form of a diagonal matrix.
other_quotes.reading: An explicit, printed recipe for injecting an externally-obtained RCS into the 38.901 channel-coefficient generator - the same two insertion points (large-scale path loss, small-scale per-path coefficient) that 3GPP eventually standardised.

other_quotes.quote: Since incident angle also affects RCS, the discrepancy between segmentation and EM-based models is quantified over multiple angles using the RMSE ... RMSE = 3.02/d + 1.76 + eps_model (d in millimetres) ... The standard deviation of delta reaches 1,82 dB in indoor office scenarios, which is significantly higher than the 1,35 dB observed in UMi environments.
other_quotes.reading: ETSI validates one RCS construction against another (segmentation vs a coupled EM model) with an RMSE over angle - a model-vs-model check, not against measurement.

the_finding_that_matters_most_to_us.quote: For further quantitative analysis, the RCS of the RIS is calculated using the physical optics method from [33], and the differences between the theoretical concatenated power and the measured power are compared. By comparing the calculated concatenated power with the actual measured power, it is observed that the difference does not exceed 7dB, with the smallest being only 0.11dB. Considering an angular measurement interval of 5 degrees, which leads to a maximum angular error of 2.5 degrees at theta_out, and given the significant fluctuation range of the RCS of RIS, a certain level of difference is considered acceptable.
the_finding_that_matters_most_to_us.reading: A PHYSICAL-OPTICS-COMPUTED sigma was injected into the standards-track target-channel path-power equation and checked against a measured channel. Spread 0.11 to 7 dB, and the authors argue the residual is explained by 2.5 degrees of angular quantisation. This is the closest published precedent for our own PO-computed sigma being taken seriously, and it also sets a realistic accuracy expectation: single-digit dB, angle-quantisation-limited.

validation_audit.question: Did the model-suppliers validate what they handed over, and against what?

rows.detail: The only validation statement printed in the TR is the Introduction pointer: 'The RCS validation results are obtained based on certain object sizes. An overview list of the sources is available in [27].' Searching the extracted text, the word 'validat' does not appear anywhere inside clause 7.9 apart from that pointer. What clause 7.9.6 provides is CALIBRATION - simulation assumptions so different companies' simulators produce the same CDFs - which is cross-implementation agreement, not a physical check of -12.81 dBsm against a held-out measurement.
rows.importance: State this precisely if we cite 3GPP. The standard's number is a consensus average, quality-controlled by inter-simulator calibration. It is not itself a validated measurement.

rows.against: a 0.5 m metal sphere for absolute calibration (closed-form RCS), and a held-out 28 GHz band predicted from a model fitted without it

channel measurements in seven indoor/outdoor scenarios; for the RIS target the injected sigma came from a PHYSICAL OPTICS calculation and the concatenated path power matched measurement to within 7 dB, best case 0.11 dB

rows.validated: NO INDEPENDENT CHECK IN THE CONTRIBUTIONS I OPENED
rows.detail: The solver outputs are presented as evidence; nothing in R1-2500660, R1-2410235 or R1-2409609 compares them against a measurement of the same airframe. Their quality control was the standards process itself: many parties' numbers were tabled side by side and averaged. The spread that survived is instructive - submitted A values for the same small-UAV size class ran from -10 dBsm (LGE) to -19.78 dBsm (Sony, CST) around the agreed -12.81 dBsm.
rows.importance: This is roughly a 10 dB spread between independent estimates of the same quantity in a standards body. It is the fairest available yardstick for what 'agreement' means in this field, and it is far looser than a reviewer might assume.

rows.against: its coupled EM cylinder model, via RMSE over angle and separation, with a fitted RMSE = 3.02/d + 1.76 (dB, d in mm); no measurement comparison in that clause
the calibration reference results reported by companies in 3GPP - i.e. agreement with other implementations, not with physics

validation_audit.the_pattern: Everyone who claims a physical validation validates the CHAIN (predicted received power or signature vs measured), not the sigma in isolation. Nobody in the standards track validates the averaged sigma against a held-out target. The one paper that validates the sigma itself is JSAC, and it does so by held-out band prediction plus sphere calibration. That defines two achievable bars for us: (bar 1) sphere/canonical-target calibration of the solver, (bar 2) end-to-end predicted-vs-measured power on a real link.

what_this_means_for_us: The user's question - has injection been published at a strong venue - now has a stronger answer than the archive sweep gave. Not only has it been published; it has been STANDARDISED. TR 38.901 clause 7.9.2.1 is an injection interface with an angle lookup and a per-path multiply, and every 6G ISAC simulator on the planet will use it.

Reposition the architecture section: our sigma grid is not 'a workaround because Sionna has no scattering integral'. It is the same layering the 3GPP ISAC channel model uses - propagation engine and target signature are separate blocks, joined by an angle-indexed sigma. What differs is only who fills the block, and 3GPP admits both measurement and ray-traced simulation (Samsung's sentence in R1-2501002).

We are FINER than the standard on both axes it collapsed: 9 x 120 angular samples versus 6 sectors, and 3 bands versus one frequency-independent number. Say so, and note that one contributor (BUPT) proposed a frequency-dependent A = 0.2133 f - 22.04 which the consensus average discarded - so frequency dependence is a known, deliberately dropped refinement, not an exotic claim.

Adopt Samsung's printed validation chain as our own framing: measurement validates the ray tracer, then the validated ray tracer validates the channel/detection model (R1-2409609, Option 2 and Proposal 24). It came from inside the standards process, so it is not something we invented to excuse ourselves.

Put -12.81 dBsm in every comparison table, but describe it correctly: '3GPP TR 38.901 V19.4.0 Table 7.9.2.1-1, small UAV, a consensus average across company measurements and simulations, frequency-independent, sigma_S std 3.74 dB'. Do NOT call it a measured value.

Use the company spread (-10 to -19.78 dBsm around -12.81 for the same size class) as the honest reference for how much disagreement is normal. If our SBR+PO grid lands within a few dB of the standard's value at a comparable aspect, that is as good as the standards body's own internal agreement.

Two adversarial points we should pre-empt: (a) Ericsson's argument that discontinuous angular RCS means the angular sampling was too coarse - our 3 degree azimuth step should be checked against a measured/simulated angular correlation length (Sony reports 6.87 degrees for a small UAV, which would make 3 degrees adequate but not generous); (b) the far-field assumption the standard states explicitly, which our chamber geometry has to satisfy per band and per airframe.

open_questions_not_opened: ITU-R WP5D IMT-2030 evaluation-methodology working documents: the draft new Report is said to introduce ISAC-specific channel models, and ATIS NGA is said to have submitted on sensing test environments to WP5D #47 (per ETSI GR ISC 002 clause 4.4.1). WP5D input documents are membership-restricted. NOT OPENED - do not claim an ITU-R RCS model exists.
ATIS Next G Alliance Phase 2 report ([i.58] in ETSI GR ISC 002), described there as including 'RCS characterization of targets such as vehicles, drones, humans, and robotic arms'. NOT OPENED.
IEEE 802.11bf / TGbf WLAN-sensing channel models - whether they define a target RCS the way 3GPP does. NOT OPENED.
The remaining RCS parameter tables in TR 38.901 (7.9.2.1-3 human model 2, -4/-5 vehicle, -6/-7 AGV) were located but not transcribed cell by cell.

Whether any strong-venue paper injects a COMMERCIAL-solver RCS table specifically into a RAY TRACER (the LAMBDA configuration) remains unresolved; the standards track uses stochastic geometry-based simulators, not ray tracers, as the consumer. The automotive-radar RT-simulator literature is the place to look next and was only skimmed in search results here, not opened.
